messages:
IncidentBot: Paging oncall: high-volume scraper spike detected hitting /v1/embeddings and /v1/chat/completions from many IPs. Traffic up 14x in last 2m, errors rising (429/503). Severity: P2.

Alex R: I’m on it. seeing large number of near-identical UA strings and rapid token usage per key. Looks like credential stuffing-ish but more like a distributed scraper trying to harvest embeddings.

Priya K: Confirmed. Top IP clusters from ASNs: AS15169, AS14618 and several small cloud providers. Most requests are small seq_len but extremely frequent.

Jamal S: Quick ask: do we have an existing WAF rule we can apply to throttle these endpoints by IP and by API key?

Alex R: Yes — we have a temp-block pattern. I’m going to push a conservative rate-limit first: per-IP 20 req/min for /v1/embeddings and 30 req/min for /v1/chat/completions. If that doesn’t drop volume, add immediate WAF block for obvious bad IPs and user agents.

Priya K: I’m patching the routing policy to prefer dedicated capacity for known customer keys so we don’t disrupt paid customers. Free/trial keys will get rate-limited more aggressively.

Alex R: Executing rate-limit via edge control plane now:
```bash
# edge-control CLI
edgectl policies create --name temp-scraper-rate --match "/v1/embeddings" --by ip --limit 20/m --scope global
edgectl policies create --name temp-chat-rate --match "/v1/chat/completions" --by ip --limit 30/m --scope global
```

IncidentBot: Policy create requests accepted (policy ids: rp-823, rp-824).

Jamal S: Looking at logs, several API keys show 10k+ calls/min — either leaked/shared keys or attackers rotating many keys. Suggest disabling bulk-download endpoints and adding stricter per-key quotas now.

Priya K: Agreed. I set per-key quota for free tier to 1000 req/day and for paid customers we keep existing quotas. Done via admin console: changed plan.default.free.quota -> 1000/day.

Alex R: WAF action next — creating temporary rule to block the top 150 IPs observed in the last 10 minutes, plus block any UA containing "ScrapeBotX" pattern.

Alex R: WAF API call:
```json
POST /waf/rules
{
  "name": "temp-scraper-block-1738214567",
  "conditions": [
    {"type":"ip_list","value":"top-150-ips-10m"},
    {"type":"ua_contains","value":"ScrapeBotX"}
  ],
  "action": "block",
  "ttl": 3600
}
```

IncidentBot: WAF rule deployed (rule id waf-1093). Blocking ~2.1m requests/min now.

Marta L: Quick check — any customer-facing errors? Support dashboard shows ~130 users reported timeouts and 18 tickets mentioning 429s in the last 6 minutes. Can we scope to only anonymous/free keys?

Priya K: I scoped the rate-limits and WAF to apply only to unverified keys and to IP ranges matching the blocked list. Paid keys are routed to dedicated capacity (no rate change). That should reduce customer impact.

Alex R: Observability: token burn dropped 60% after WAF + rate-limits. Error rate normalized from 8.2% -> 1.4%. Latency for /v1/embeddings returned to baseline within 90s for paid customers, a bit higher for free tier.

Jamal S: Noted pattern: many requests used the same prompt template with slight param tweaks. I’m snapshotting the example request for an eval rule.

Priya K: I posted a short status note to status.redwood.com: "Investigating elevated traffic and errors on embeddings & chat. Mitigations in place. Some free-tier customers may see rate limits. Paid customers unaffected." Link: https://status.redwood.com/incident/1738214567

Support Bot: Auto-response sent to customers with recent 429s offering ETA and workaround instructions (rotate key, contact support for emergency quota).

Marta L: Handoff time for next oncall in 20m. Alex/Jamal — please summarize open items for me to take over.

Alex R: Open items:
- Keep WAF rule waf-1093 for 1h and monitor false positives.
- Maintain per-ip limits rp-823 / rp-824.
- Revisit if we need to escalate to blocking entire ASNs.
- Validate no paid keys are affected (audit logs show none so far).
- Coordinate with Support for any SLA escalations.

Jamal S: I’ll keep an eye on token burn and submit a follow-up if we see attacker pivot to paid keys. Also will prepare a list of top 50 IPs to escalate to upstream provider if necessary.

Marta L: OK taking over. My plan: keep rules as-is, run a 15-min false-positive scan against customer IP lists, and set alert if errors >2% for paid customers. I’ll escalate to infra if we see cross-region propagation.

Alex R: FYI I already opened a low-priority postmortem draft and pinned the relevant logs: /logs/incidents/1738214567/scraper-spike.log.

Priya K: Closing loop with Support: we replied to top 10 tickets with targeted instructions and offered temporary quota increases where customers showed business-critical impact.

Marta L: Thanks team. I’ll let IncidentBot know when we can remove waf-1093 and the temp rate-limits. For now, we keep mitigations until traffic is back to baseline for 30m.

IncidentBot: Acknowledged. Auto-check scheduled: in 15m (1738215775) to evaluate traffic and error rates.

Alex R: Quick note for runbook: if attacker moves to paid keys, step sequence is: 1) re-route suspected keys to a sandboxed node, 2) force rotate keys + notify customers, 3) escalate to sales/support for compensatory credits.

Marta L: End-of-handoff: I’m now oncall primary. If anything changes ping @Marta L; I’ll update the status page as needed. :white_check_mark:

Support Bot: Handoff summary posted to #support with links to WAF rule waf-1093, policies rp-823/rp-824, and log snapshot.

Alex R: Thanks. I’m going to clean up the temp policies after we’re stable.

Jamal S: Monitoring continues. If any of you see new UA patterns, DM me.

Marta L: Closing thread for now; will re-open if mitigations need to escalate.
